@graph.description: Your website may be delivering more requests than your business can answer. Here are the seven handoffs between a quote request and a signed job, the verified failure rate at each one, the arithmetic that turns seven tolerable leaks into a 20% win rate, and the 90-minute audit you can run from four exports you already own.

about.name: Lead intake path audit — a seven-handoff review of what happens to a quote request between website form submission and a recorded outcome, measured for a Metro Detroit service business with one phone line, one inbox, and a quote log: form completion (Zuko 2025 benchmarking, 34% of starters abandon), acknowledgement, phone answer rate (Invoca 2026 at 56%, CallRail 2026 at 28% unanswered, and the 2016 origin of the widely repeated 62% figure), hold time, speed to first response (2007 MIT/InsideSales lead response study with its sample and sponsor limits stated), quote turnaround, follow-up cadence (1.3 attempts average versus six attempts), and whether the outcome is logged at all. Includes the compounding arithmetic across seven handoffs, four exports a business already owns, six fixes ranked by effort, and where Chainlink Runtime Environment verified workflows and on-premises Local LLM drafting fit.

mainEntity.name: What is a lead intake audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a stage-by-stage measurement of what happens to a quote request between submission and a recorded outcome — form completion, acknowledgement, answer rate, time to first response, quote turnaround, follow-up attempts, and whether the outcome was logged. It measures the business, not the website.

mainEntity.name: What percentage of business calls go unanswered?

acceptedAnswer.text: CallRail's 2026 platform data puts it at 28%, and Invoca's 2026 benchmark finds 56% of calls reach a person at all, rising to 65% for calls over 15 seconds. The widely repeated 62% figure comes from a 2016 study of 85 businesses that counted voicemail as unanswered.

mainEntity.name: How fast should a business respond to a website inquiry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Automated acknowledgement should be under a minute, and a human response should come within one business hour. The 2007 MIT/InsideSales study found leads called within five minutes were 21 times more likely to qualify, though it measured contact and qualification from six companies — direction, not a guarantee.

mainEntity.name: How many times should you follow up on a quote?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six attempts across call, text, and email. InsideSales research puts the average at 1.3 attempts, which means most quotes are abandoned by the seller, not rejected by the buyer.

mainEntity.name: What is a normal form abandonment rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zuko's 2025 benchmark of 93 million form sessions found 34% of people who start a form never complete it. Anything materially above that points at field count, mobile layout, or the lack of an obvious next step.
